$comment: Every field is a measurement with its method, or the literal string "not measured", or "blocked: <what>".
device: web · Chromium 1440x950 · Apple silicon, WebGPU. NOT a device tier: no phone or tablet capture exists yet.

blinkRatePerMin.method: IdleEngine.step at 60Hz for 20 min, seeded, counting blinkStarted. Counted at the generator because the renderer neither adds nor drops a blink; blink TIMING relative to speech is blinkNearPausePct and is not this number. Target 12-20: inside it.

breathRatePerMin.method: Intervals between breathStarted flags over a seeded 20 min run at 60Hz. Target 12-20: inside it. Cycle-to-cycle period variation 15.0% against the +/-15% asked for. The earlier 7.4% was two faults: the engine drew a fresh RATE each cycle from the 12-16/min range, which caps variation at 0.07/sqrt(3) ~ 8.7% by construction, and the measurement counted zero-crossings of breathY, whose interval spans parts of two consecutive cycles and averages their periods (15% generated read back as 12.3%). Session mean and per-cycle jitter are now separate numbers, and the cycle boundary is observable.

measurements.interruptVoiceStopMs: blocked: needs a device — the JS path in tutor-audio.ts stop() is synchronous, so what remains to measure is the audio hardware buffer flush

interruptSettleMs.method: Time for the speech swell (the envelope the arms and brow ride on) to fall below 0.05 after `speaking` goes false, at 60Hz seeded. Full decay profile: 117 ms to half, 400 ms to 0.1, 500 ms to 0.05, 783 ms to 0.01. Target 700 ms: inside it at the 0.05 threshold. Measured on the ENVELOPE, not the pose — differencing a run that stopped speaking against one that never spoke does not work, because speech boosts the blink hazard and shortens saccade intervals, so the two consume different draws from the shared seeded stream and never reconverge (0.275 deg divergence at the cut against a 0.120 deg residual floor, curve non-monotonic at 130% recovered one second in). BODY HALF ONLY: the audio stopping is interruptVoiceStopMs and needs a device.

frameTimeP95Ms.method: requestAnimationFrame deltas in-page over 40s of idle, 2401 frames, taken in a pass with no screenshots running: a screenshot stalls the compositor, so a series captured alongside one measures the harness. p50 16.70, p95 17.70, p99 18.30 — vsync-locked at 60Hz with no long frames. This is the web tier only.

idlePeriodicityPeak.method: Autocorrelation peak past the first zero crossing, on motion measured from the COMPOSITED frame (fraction of pixels changing >2 grey levels between full-resolution screenshots, 14.9/s over 40s). Peak sits at 12.6s; against 200 AR(1) surrogates fitted to the signal's own smoothness, p=0.070 — not distinguishable from a smooth aperiodic signal. The surrogates carry a 500-sample burn-in so they reach stationary variance before the series starts, and a surrogate whose autocorrelation never crosses zero is counted as at least as extreme as the observation rather than as the minimum; without those two the same capture reads p=0.025, which is anti-conservative. Not comparable to the generator's own coefficient, which measures 0.74 for the same underlying motion.

backchannelCuesTraceable.method: Cue-driven by construction: src/idle/engine.ts starts a nod only on partnerPauseEvent || partnerF0Falling while !speechActive, under a 2.2 s refractory — the periodic timer-nod was removed (the constructor still burns its PRNG draw so the seeded face stream stays where it was). Verified behaviourally, not just by reading: 20 min at 60 Hz, engine default seed, 134 scripted partnerPauseEvent pulses (one every 18 s plus an echo 0.8 s later, inside the refractory, so ≤ is exercised rather than =) → 67 nod onsets, every one ≤2 frames after a cue. The onset detector is calibrated to the waveform: nodPitch samples exactly 0 on the cue frame itself (sin(0)), so onset lags its cue by one frame, and the zero between the two nods of a sequence lasts exactly one frame at 60 Hz (nodS 0.35 s = 21 frames) and is not an onset. The 67 echo cues correctly produced nothing. Cue-free control run: 0 onsets in 20 min. ENGINE ONLY: this traces nodPitch at the generator; whether the app layer raises partnerPauseEvent at real turn ends is a different question and is not covered here.
backchannelCuesTraceable.capture: .claude/skills/presence-metrics/scripts/nod-traceability.mts: 134 cues → 67 nods, 0 untraceable; control 0 cues → 0 nods

value.selfIntersections: blocked: no mesh or collision representation exists in this Node harness (bones only, no skinned geometry) — a proxy would be an invented number

artifactsIn20MinCapture.method: 20 simulated minutes at 60 Hz, seed 7, quiet input, on the real natalie.gltf bone hierarchy built the way feet.test.ts builds it. Per frame: pose reset = any bone's LOCAL rotation moving >10° in one frame; foot slide = DEF-toe.L/R horizontal drift >2 mm (the feet gate's bound) from rest — or, under a clip at full blend, from the toe's position at entry into the clip's own contacts window, because rest-anchored drift would count the clip's real foot repositions as slide (mid-fade the base is a mix and slide is not evaluated); eye detachment = DEF-eye.L/R in the DEF-spine.006 (head) frame drifting >1 mm from its rest offset. Two passes: presence alone, and a base cycling setBaseClip(idle_19,0) → after its duration setBaseClip(null) → 5 s → idle_21 → 5 s → wei_rl_45 → repeat, clips regenerated via node tools/retarget_staystill.mjs --all-curated. Quiet pass: 1/0/0 — the one reset is frame 0 only, the first step snapping the fingers from glTF rest into the engine's relaxed-hand baseline (worst 21.0°, DEF-f_pinky.02.L); worst slide 0.458 mm (the feet test's known skin-blend residual), worst eye drift 0.31 mm. Clip pass: 10/0/21, and two FINDINGS, reported rather than widened away: (a) 9 of the 10 resets (18 of 19 frames) are the LOOP SEAM — playback wrapping from the last frame to frame 0 jumps DEF-forearm.L 12.0° on every idle_19 pass and 26.1° on every wei_rl_45 pass; the curation's loop-closure criteria bound hips and ankles, not arms, so any looping playback of these clips hits this. Cross-fade interpolation itself never registered: the single mid-fade-flagged frame is the second half of a seam jump landing on the first fade-out frame. (b) Eye detachment exists only under a clip base: 21 events / 466 frames, worst 2.44 mm at blend 0.50 fading out of wei_rl_45, with marginal 1.0–1.2 mm excursions at full blend during the idles — the twin translation tracks carry most but not all of the head-frame offset through fades. Foot slide never fired in either pass. Self-intersection is NOT counted, for the stated reason. GENERATOR-SIDE: this is the bone hierarchy in Node, not a rendered capture — skinning, morphs and the GPU path are not covered.
